reforms.description: Japan employs direct research in national organisations, financing of private sector research through the Fiscal Investment and Loan Program, tax privileges for R&D expenditure, and subsidies to basic research such as development of new energy technologies as major policy instruments for research and development promotion.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Public R&D funding and tax incentives for private research support innovation capacity and human capital development, raising long-term productivity and technological competitiveness.
reforms.status_evidence: The text describes these as existing 'major policy instruments for research and development promotion' in Japan, indicating they are in force.
reforms.importance_rationale: These are established, multi-instrument R&D support mechanisms spanning both public and private sectors. While not a new structural reform, they represent significant ongoing policy commitment to research and development across basic and applied domains.
reforms.source_quote: Major policy instruments for research and development promotion are: Direct research in national organisations; Financing private sector research through the Fiscal Investment and Loan Program; Tax privileges for R&D expenditure, and subsidies to basic research such as development of new energy technologies.
